subject: koala
pitch: A sleepy koala hugging a eucalyptus branch. Soft ash-grey fur with a cream chest and cream-lined fluffy ears, a big black leathery nose, half-closed drowsy brown eyes, strong grey paws with dark claws, and a sprig of blue-green eucalyptus leaves in one hand, mid-munch.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module using only the SDK's exported functions, aiming for a realistically-scaled sitting koala (~0.7m) hugging a branch, with helper functions for randomness and surface painting like mottling and countershading.

Now I'm working out coordinates and geometry: the koala sits on a diagonal eucalyptus branch whose base touches the ground, with the branch built as a swept path with bark coloring, positioned so the koala's seat rests around y≈0.35 while the whole model still stands on y=0.

Actually, placing the branch in front risks blocking the face, so I'll shift it to the koala's side instead — a leaning stem rising at roughly x≈-0.22 past the body, letting the arms wrap around it while the koala still faces forward.

Writing branch curve points...

Now moving to the koala's body shape, thinking of it as a rounded sitting bulk.

For the body, I'll build a spine chain of joints running from hips up through the torso to the neck, then loft the body mesh along that chain with varying width and height stations to get the wide, round koala silhouette.

For the head, I'll attach a sphere geometry sized to roughly 0.13 radius to the head joint, positioning it via explicit local coordinates since the loft frame's attachment point needs world-space placement.

For scaling into an ellipsoid, I'll skip the risky part-option scale parameter and instead call .scale() directly on the sphere geometry itself, which is more reliable. For the ears, I'm planning large round fluffy spheres flattened on one axis for the fur color, with a smaller cream-colored sphere layered on top as the inner ear lining.

Positioning the ears symmetrically on the head bone using a left/right multiplier, then moving to the eyes: a dark brown sphere for the eyeball with a fur-colored eyelid sphere covering the upper half to give that drowsy, half-closed koala look.

Now I'm figuring out eye placement on the head sphere, aiming for the front-side position a koala's eyes would sit, roughly at x=s*0.065, y=0.76, z=0.2, checking against the head's radius to find the right surface point.

For the nose, I'm placing a large dark leathery shape slightly below center on the face, using a scaled sphere flattened into an ellipsoid at around y=0.725, z=0.215, colored near-black.

Then I'm adding a cream-colored chest patch as a flattened ellipsoid embedded into the body's front surface near y=0.47.

Realizing the loft geometry only controls width and height per cross-section, not raw depth, so positioning the chest ellipsoid precisely by z-coordinate is unreliable—I'm shifting toward using a paint function instead, coloring the body cream wherever z and y fall within the chest region, which sidesteps the depth-placement problem entirely.

Now I'm working through the arm geometry for the koala wrapping around the branch, estimating shoulder, elbow, and paw positions so the hand lands on the branch's surface, and considering using an IK limb function to hit that target precisely rather than hardcoding joint positions.

I'll build the arm chain from three limb points (shoulder, elbow, wrist), naming them so the last one becomes the tip joint for the hand, then attach the chain to the spine as its parent. For the paw itself, I'm planning a scaled sphere at the wrist tip with small cone shapes for claws.

For positioning, I'm placing the left arm so the hand reaches near the mouth holding a eucalyptus sprig, checking shoulder-to-hand distance stays within the limb's total reach. Then I'm sketching a leaf outline shape to extrude for the eucalyptus leaves, using a lance-like silhouette in grey-blue-green tones.

Now I'm working out the sprig itself: a curved stem swept from the hand toward the mouth, with several leaves spaced along it at fractional points, each oriented with perpendicular x/y directions computed via interpolation along the stem path.

I won't stress too much about exact orthogonality since any skew should be minor—I'll just pick direction vectors with small dot products and move on. Maybe simpler to use a flat extruded shape for the leaves instead of overcomplicating the geometry.

Now I'm working out the koala's sitting pose: hips rooted around y=0.2-0.25, with the rump resting near the ground and feet positioned forward. For the hind legs I'm setting up a two-joint limb chain from hip to foot, checking that the bend direction (angled forward and up at the knee) and limb lengths are enough to reach the foot target without overextending—confirming the distance is comfortably within the limb's max reach.

Now I'm placing the feet with small claw spikes, positioning the ears on the head sphere's surface so they slightly overlap into the head for a natural attached look, adding a cream-colored inner ear patch, and setting up the head joint attached without its own aim direction so it inherits the neck's orientation.

I'm now building the skeleton hierarchy: a hips root joint, a three-joint spine chain curving upward via catmull points, a neck/head joint attached to the spine tip, and a lofted body mesh skinned across the spine chain using the mottled color material.

I'm sketching loft cross-sections for the body at hip, belly, chest, and shoulder heights, reasoning through whether width and height should map to the x and z axes of the spine's local frame so the koala's torso reads as roughly circular and proportioned correctly front-to-back.

The cream chest patch gets painted onto surface points with higher z and within the belly-to-shoulder height range. I'm skipping a tail since koalas don't have a visible one, then working out the branch's position and radius taper, deciding to pull it closer to the body so the arm can plausibly reach it, and planning to sweep it along a curved path anchored to the nearest joint.

I'll add bark texture via a grain paint pattern along the branch's length, and consider sprouting a few small leaves off it for detail. For the arms, I'm rooting them off a shoulder joint on the spine and building each as a limb chain from that shoulder point to a hand target.

Now I'm working out the geometry for both arms and legs: computing shoulder-to-hand distances against the segment lengths to confirm they fit, setting elbow bend directions, and placing the right paw so it wraps around the front of the branch without clipping into the body. Checking that the branch sits outside the body's silhouette at that height confirms the pose reads correctly, and now I'm positioning the hind hip joints next.

Adding claws to the paws, positioning spikes near the foot tip and binding them to the ankle bone so they move rigidly with the foot.

Now I'm mapping out joint naming conventions -- left side uses "L" suffix, with arm chains (shoulder, elbow, wrist) parented to the spine and leg chains parented to the hips. Next I need to attach eyes, nose, ears, and a mouth to the head bone.

For the eyes, I'm placing small dark brown spheres as eyeballs, then adding a half-cap sphere over the top as a drooping eyelid to give the koala a drowsy look -- covering roughly the top half while leaving the lower portion of the eyeball visible.

I'm positioning a black ellipsoid nose on the lower-front muzzle, and sketching a paint rule that shades the head cream in the lower-front muzzle region versus the darker fur elsewhere.

Now I'm defining the color palette and material system — a mottled grey fur, cream chest, dark nose and claws, warm brown eyes, and bark/leaf tones for the environment — then setting up how each body part gets painted with these mottled textures. I'm working out the imports needed for the build, including the mottle and paint utilities for generating the koala's textured surfaces.

Setting up builder skeleton...

Adding head paint logic and sphere geometry for the skull, then starting the ear parts loop...

Adjusting eyelid positioning...

Setting up arm chains...

Checking the hind leg geometry — hip to knee to foot distances fit within the segment lengths, and I'm setting the knee bend to point forward so the leg flexes naturally toward the foot target.

Now I'm attaching the paw sphere at the leg tip and scaling it slightly for a flattened foot shape, then placing three small claw spikes angled downward-forward along the front edge of each paw, sized small enough to look proportional on a 5cm paw.

For the hands, I'm positioning the left wrist to hold the sprig and the right wrist to grip the branch, adjusting the right paw's offset so it nestles against the branch surface with minimal gap given their respective radii, and adding matching claw spikes to each hand angled toward the branch.

For the limbs, I'm checking that the bend distance between shoulder root and hand target fits the arm's two segment lengths, which gives a strongly bent elbow pose typical of how koalas cling — fine for the pose, with elbows angling outward and down.

Now I'm working out the eucalyptus sprig: a bezier stem running from the holding hand up toward the mouth area, attached near the wrist bone, and I'm starting to plan leaf placements by sampling points along that bezier curve.

Defining leaf outline points...

Still working on leaf geometry — placing six leaves at increasing points along the stem, alternating sides, and figuring out the perpendicular axis for each leaf's orientation using the stem's tangent direction.

Still computing leaf orientation vectors...

Now I'm setting up the branch's bark sweep path with a catmull curve from ground to tip, defining its radius profile and flat-to-round end caps.

I'm also planning leaf clusters along the branch at a few points for lushness, and factoring out a reusable leaf helper function that builds a leaf's orientation from a direction vector using cross products.

Working out branch leaf placement...

rng(seed) returns a generator function I can call repeatedly, so I'll grab `rand = rng(7)` and call it for randomness. I'm positioning the branch leaves away from the body on the -x side so they don't clash with the arm, and double-checking the spine joint chain, head placement, and hip role assignments for the koala's skeleton.

I'm now working through the loft geometry for the hind legs and body — making sure the hip joints sit where the body's bottom actually meets the ground rather than floating above it. I need to figure out whether the loft's width/height map to x/z or y, since for a vertical spine chain the normal and binormal likely correspond to depth and width rather than vertical height, which changes how I should set the station positions to get the koala sitting properly on the ground.

I realize the spine chain and loft stations need to align, so I'm reworking the hips joint position and spine path to match the body loft stations, simplifying by placing the hips root lower and adjusting station heights/widths along the y-axis from the base up to the shoulders.

I'm checking that nothing floats above the floor and working through limb distances—legs, arms, and the sprig branch with leaves attached using bezier curves, tangent-based leaf orientation, and alternating leaf types. I'm also planning the claw spikes on the paws (gripping the branch and resting on the ground), the eyes and eyelids on the head joint, and making sure every part gets a color before assembling the final build function with joints, loft body, limb chains, and foliage attachments.
